# §5 Commerce Analytics — Highlight Candidates

1. **39.9% GMV capture from 8.5% of orders** — eCat captures nearly 40% of all-channel business value through fewer than 1 in 10 orders, with a 4.7× AOV premium ($8,994 vs $1,908) over the trailing 12 months. [→ §commerce]
2. **Top-5 buyer concentration at 39%** — The five largest eCat buyers account for 39% of platform GMV (trailing 12 months), with The Parker Company alone representing 22% on just 28 orders. [→ §commerce]
3. **Quote-dominant workflow drives value** — 74.7% of eCat orders are quotes averaging $10,582, 2.5× the value of confirmed orders, confirming the platform's role as a project specification tool (trailing 12 months). [→ §commerce]
4. **Top eCat buyers absent from largest all-channel accounts** — None of the top 10 eCat buyers appear among the highest-volume all-channel customers, indicating eCat serves a distinct project-focused segment while major distributors remain unactivated (trailing 12 months). [→ §commerce]

## Priority Action Candidate
- **MEDIUM**: Expanding eCat order capture from 8.5% toward the GMV capture rate of 39.9% could potentially add $8–10M in annual platform GMV by bringing mid-value transactions onto the platform — the 4.7× AOV gap suggests reps are only using eCat for their largest orders while processing routine business through other channels [HYPOTHETICAL]. [→ §commerce]
